faq.a: Sultan is associated with the Arabic form سُلْطَان, whose core sense is sultan; ruler, authority.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sultan?
faq.a: Sultan is associated with Arabic. Sultan is Arabic سُلْطَان (Sulṭān), meaning 'ruler, authority'.
Yes — the underlying form سُلْطَان is Arabic.
Sultan can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sultan should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ل ط is Quranic (authority), but Sulṭān is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sultan mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sultan is rendered سلطان and carries the sense سلطان، حاکم.

faq.q: What does Sultan mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sultan is rendered سلطان and carries the sense سلطان، فرمانروا.
A romanized syllable approximation is sul-tan. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sultan?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sultan, sultan. Script forms are سلطان, سُلْطَان, सुल्तान.

faq.q: Is Sultan a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
